rounds.text: Hariyana Ship Breakers Ltd is trading at a deep discount, anchored by a remarkably low price-to-earnings ratio of 3.54x [E1] and a price-to-book ratio of just 0.41x, with shares priced at ₹ 99.0 against a book value of ₹ 239 [E2]. This significant undervaluation relative to fundamental asset backing is further magnified by a blistering inflection in top-line performance, evidenced by a compounded sales growth of 1567% over the trailing twelve months [E16]. This explosive revenue acceleration has triggered a fundamental turnaround where profit growth exceeds one-year price growth by 751%, indicating that the market has completely failed to price in the company's surging earnings momentum [E53]. The broader valuation multiples also signal severe mispricing when benchmarked against industry peers, showing the stock's P/E at 15.25x against a sector benchmark of 23.4x and its P/B at 0.43x compared to a sector benchmark of 2.64x [E6, E7]. Conceded: historical sales growth paints a grim long-term picture with compounded figures of -53% over 5 years and -60% over 3 years [E14, E15]. Conceded: the business struggles with low profitability metrics, including a negative return on assets of -2.15% and a median return on equity of 3% over the past 5 years [E8, E25].

The bull case relies heavily on low surface-level valuation multiples such as a price-to-book ratio of 0.41x [E2] and a P/E of 3.54 [E1], but these metrics mask deep structural weakness in profitability and capital allocation. Return on assets sits firmly in negative territory at -2.15% against a healthy sector benchmark of 4.95% [E8], demonstrating that the underlying assets are actively destroying value rather than generating productive returns. Furthermore, historical profitability is chronically depressed, evidenced by a miserable median return on equity of just 3% over the past five years [E25] and a meager 3.62% over the last three years [E60]. Top-line performance reveals an alarming secular decay rather than a stable compounding business, highlighted by a catastrophic compounded sales growth rate of -53% over five years [E14] and -60% over three years [E15]. Shareholders receive zero compensation for enduring these depressed operational metrics, as the dividend yield stands at an absolute 0.00% [E4]. Conceded: the trailing twelve months show an isolated surge in sales growth of 1567% [E16] alongside short-term profit growth screening triggers [E64], yet this volatility occurs against a backdrop of long-term value destruction and low multi-year returns.

Conceded: the 5-year sales growth is -53% [E14] and the 3-year median return on equity is a low 3.62% [E60]. However, the bear's focus on historical decay ignores a massive structural inflection point: compounded sales growth over the trailing twelve months has surged by 1567% [E16]. This explosive turnaround is further reinforced by fundamental signals indicating that profit growth exceeds 1-year price growth by 751% [E53]. Far from a business actively destroying value, earnings growth is actively accelerating [E66] and driving a rock-bottom P/E ratio of just 3.54 [E1] that makes the current ₹ 61.0 Cr market capitalization [E3] deeply disconnected from this fundamental momentum.

Conceded: compounded sales growth over the trailing twelve months is 1567% [E16]. However, the bull's reliance on this single TTM surge ignores a devastating multi-year structural contraction, namely a 5-year compounded sales growth of -53% [E14] and a 3-year compounded sales growth of -60% [E15]. This makes the TTM spike look like a volatile anomaly rather than a stable turnaround. Furthermore, pointing to a P/E of 3.54 [E1] and an accelerating earnings screen [E66] overlooks the chronic, anemic profitability that underpins this business: a 10-year median return on equity of 4% [E24], a 5-year median return on equity of 3% [E25], and a recent low ROE of 7% [E67]. The company also generates a negative return on assets (ROA) of -2.15% against a sector benchmark of 4.95% [E8], proving that even with headline earnings growth, asset efficiency remains deeply impaired. Finally, investors see zero cash return for taking on this volatility, as the dividend yield sits firmly at 0.00% [E4].
